insights.insight: The protocol delivers cryptographic proof of purchase at ~$0.10 per receipt versus $5–$150 for probabilistic ad-tech attribution — a 50–200x cost differential with no pixel, no lookback window, and no inference model to calibrate.

7-day GMV rose 2.8% to $74,397 while receipt count fell from 1,777 to 1,619 — meaning spend per verified transaction is increasing even as throughput softens. For brands, this signals the active buyer pool is skewing toward higher-value purchases.

Transaction velocity has held at 0.63–0.67x for three consecutive readings after a 0.593x low — it has not returned to the 0.70–0.75x range seen earlier. Brands planning on volume-based targeting at scale should treat current throughput as the working baseline, not a floor before a rebound.

Amazon, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, and three OpenAI receipt domains are among the 10 DKIM-verified vendors — meaning verified purchase data already spans SaaS, AI tools, and marketplace commerce, not just physical retail.

Cumulative average basket sits at $59.69 against a long-run ~$80 baseline — a compression of roughly 25% that has persisted across readings. Audience segments built on this data will skew toward mid-market spend behavior, not premium.

Active CBSAs held flat at 14 with zero new metro entries this period. Marketers requiring broad geographic reach should verify whether their target DMAs are represented before building activation plans against this data.
